notes:
**A customer locked out by a network failure was told to check the wrong
vendor.** Every shipped build is licensed through one provider, chosen when the
build is stamped — but one error message named the other one, hardcoded. A buyer
whose first activation could not reach the network was sent to a service that
had never issued their key.

This was found after a sibling product lost a real sale to exactly that
confusion. That product's cause was different — it asked one provider, failed on
a network error, and never asked the second. Docket cannot do that: it contacts
exactly one provider per build, decided before the binary ships, with no
fallback path between them. That is now asserted by a test rather than assumed,
so a future change introducing a two-provider sequence fails.

**A server error no longer bills two jobs.** When a run of URLs came back with
the same stand-in body under HTTP 500, the report listed them at CRITICAL as
server errors and again as a separate task worth 6.5 points, whose advice sent
the reader hunting a bot-management rule for pages their own server was erroring
on. The observation stays on the record; the duplicate job does not.
